2. A block of mass 3 kg is in contact with a second block of mass 2 kg, both resting on a frictionless floor. A horizontal force F = 10N is applied to push the first block. Find the force with which the first block pushes the second block.

Solution: Since two bodies are in touch, 10N force applied goes to push both the blocks. Therefore, a= F/m⇒ 10/ (3+2) = 2 ms-1. Now the pushing force to the second block = m×a = 2×2 = 4N 3. As a result, you experience a backward force during the recoil of the bullet. iv) You feel more hurt to go for a day-long walk along a pitched road rather than along the grassy runway. v) You feel safer sitting on a sofa rather than on a wooden bench. You get severely hurt while beating the cemented wall rather than a soft wall. vi) In all these outlined tasks, two forces arise in opposite directions and always occur in pairs. The backward force initiated first in each task, such as throwing water, recoil force on the body during firing, pushing back the ground on jumping and walking, and pressing backward against benches, are the action forces. The forward-oriented forces in motion are the reaction forces. The pitched road and the cemented walls exert sufficient reaction forces that cause more severe injury. From the study of such activities, Newton again formulated a new law which is known as the Newton’s third law of motion.

Statement: To every action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction. Newton’s third law states that when two bodies interact, they apply forces to one another that are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. The third law is also known as the law of action and reaction. In the fig, mg is the downward weight of the load on the table and R is the reaction force.
By the third law, R = -mg Physics, Grade 11 | 81

Fig4.2: Showing the Third Law In the third law, action generally occurs in backwards motion while reaction proceeds onwards. Action is given to a body and the body in turn provides the reaction to the action giving body. Hence the action and reaction act on two different bodies and they never cancel. Q: Action and reaction forces are equal and opposite but they never cancel, why?
